job.title: Payroll Officer
job.description:
About the Organisation

This well-established Australian business with a significant operational footprint and a strong focus on quality, continuous improvement and delivering exceptional outcomes.

With a large and diverse workforce, the business offers a fast-paced, hands-on environment where collaboration, accuracy and a commitment to service are highly valued.

About the Role

Reporting to the People & Culture Manager, you will be responsible for delivering accurate and compliant payroll processing, ensuring employee records, time and attendance data, and payroll transactions are maintained to a high standard.

Working closely with operational leaders, HR and Finance, you will play an important role in ensuring employees are paid correctly and on time, while providing responsive support and resolving payroll queries.
Key responsibilities will include:
  • Maintaining accurate time and attendance records, including overtime, leave and employee entitlements.
  • Managing new employee setups, payroll adjustments, deductions and termination payments.
  • Validating labour hire hours and supplier invoices.
  • Preparing superannuation payments and maintaining accurate payroll and personnel records.
  • Responding to employee payroll queries and resolving discrepancies in a timely manner.
  • Partnering with operational leaders to ensure accurate timekeeping and overtime approvals.
  • Supporting payroll reporting, compliance and continuous improvement initiatives.
About You

You will be an experienced Payroll Officer who enjoys working in a busy, operationally focused environment and takes pride in delivering accurate, timely outcomes.

You bring strong attention to detail, sound knowledge of payroll legislation and the confidence to work with a range of stakeholders to resolve issues and meet competing deadlines.

To be successful, you will demonstrate:
  • Strong knowledge of Australian payroll legislation, Enterprise Agreements and relevant employment conditions.
  • Ideally experience using Kronos, ADP and SAP.
  • Demonstrated experience managing time and attendance, payroll adjustments, leave entitlements and termination payments.
  • Excellent attention to detail, organisational skills and the ability to meet strict payroll deadlines.
  • Strong communication and problem-solving skills, with a customer-focused approach.
  • A proactive, flexible and collaborative working style.
Experience supporting payroll within a large, complex or operationally focused workforce will be highly regarded.

About Applying

If you are an experienced Payroll Officer looking for a hands-on role within a collaborative People & Culture team, we would welcome your application.

To learn more, please reach out to Eliza Kennedy at ekennedy@thenextstep.com.au or apply now.

job.title: Head of People & Culture - Geelong
job.description:
A unique opportunity has arisen for an experienced and commercially minded People & Culture leader to join a purpose-led organisation experiencing significant growth across multiple sectors. With a workforce of approximately 600 employees and contractors across Australia and offshore locations, the business is on an exciting path of expansion through acquisition, with a long-term vision to scale substantially over the coming years.

This is a rare opportunity to shape and execute the people strategy within a complex, entrepreneurial environment where growth, transformation and innovation are front and centre. We're looking for a People & Culture leader who thinks like a founder, acts like a builder, and can create the people infrastructure required to support rapid organisational growth.

The Opportunity
Reporting directly to the executive leadership team, this role carries a dual mandate: providing strategic leadership across People & Culture while ensuring operational excellence across a geographically dispersed workforce.
Initially offered as a 12-month fixed-term contract with a completion bonus, the role is expected to evolve into a permanent executive-level position, with a clear pathway toward a future Chief People Officer appointment.
Based in Geelong, you will play a pivotal role in building people frameworks, integrating acquired businesses, developing offshore capability, and creating scalable systems that support rapid organisational growth.

Key Responsibilities
  • Develop and execute the first year of a broader three-year People & Culture strategy
  • Partner with senior leaders to establish strategic workforce and people priorities
  • Design and implement a scalable acquisition onboarding and integration model
  • Lead organisational change initiatives associated with rapid growth and business acquisitions
  • Implement and embed performance management frameworks across multiple business units
  • Establish and optimise offshore workforce models and international team structures
  • Develop and manage the People & Culture budget and operating plan
  • Provide leadership, coaching and support to an established P&C team
  • Drive continuous improvement across systems, processes, reporting and workforce data
  • Build the people foundations, capability and workforce plans required to support future growth and scalability
About You
You are a hands-on People & Culture leader who thrives in fast-paced, founder-led environments. You bring an entrepreneurial mindset, enjoy building from the ground up, and have the foresight to create people strategies, systems and structures that support growth before the business outgrows them.

Comfortable navigating ambiguity, you can think strategically, make decisions at pace and quickly translate ideas into action. You are equally comfortable in the boardroom discussing strategy as you are rolling up your sleeves to deliver outcomes.

You may already be operating at Head of People & Culture level, or be a high-performing senior P&C leader who has successfully delivered many of the responsibilities associated with a Head of People role and is ready to take the next step in your career. Experience within for-purpose, community services or other mission-driven organisations will be highly regarded, however we are equally interested in leaders who have built scalable people functions in other complex, growth-oriented sectors.

You Will Bring
  • Demonstrated success leading People & Culture initiatives within high-growth, complex, multi-site or multi-entity organisations
  • An entrepreneurial, founder-style mindset with the ability to identify opportunities, solve problems proactively and build scalable solutions in rapidly evolving environments
  • Strong project management and execution capability, with the ability to develop strategy and rapidly translate it into practical outcomes
  • Experience supporting acquisitions, integration programs, organisational transformation or significant change initiatives
  • Exposure to complex industrial relations environments, including experience interpreting and managing multiple modern awards and enterprise agreements
  • Experience establishing, leading or scaling offshore and international teams
  • A commercial, data-led approach to workforce planning, reporting and decision-making
  • Strong systems capability, with experience implementing or optimising HR technology, processes and frameworks to support organisational growth
  • The ability to think ahead, anticipate future workforce and capability requirements, and build the foundations required for long-term scale
  • Experience gained within for-purpose, community services, healthcare, disability, aged care, retail, hospitality or other complex workforce environments
  • The confidence to challenge thinking, influence stakeholders and build capability across the organisation
  • The ambition and capability to step into your first formal Head of People & Culture role, or leverage existing executive-level people leadership experience to make a broader organisational impact
What's on Offer
  • Opportunity to shape the people strategy of a rapidly growing organisation
  • Significant exposure to acquisitions, transformation and organisational design
  • Executive visibility and influence across the business
  • Strong career progression with a pathway to a future Chief People Officer role
  • Flexible benefits including salary packaging options
  • Attractive remuneration package, including completion bonus
Apply Now
This opportunity will suit an ambitious People & Culture leader who is energised by growth, transformation and the opportunity to build something meaningful. If you have the commercial acumen, entrepreneurial mindset and execution capability to help scale a purpose-led organisation through its next phase of growth, please apply now

job.title: HR Business Partner - Growth & Intergration

Working within a high-performing corporate People & Culture team, you'll partner closely with acquisition, transition and operational leaders to support newly acquired businesses through post-acquisition integration.

This is not a traditional operational HRBP role.

The acquired businesses retain ownership of their day-to-day people management activities. Your focus is to provide governance, guidance, workforce compliance oversight and strategic people support, ensuring alignment to group standards while helping leaders navigate change successfully.

With acquisitions ranging from 50 to 500 employees and new opportunities emerging regularly, no two months will look the same.

  • Leading people-related acquisition and integration activities
  • Workforce compliance, awards, contracts and governance alignment
  • HRIS, employee data and payroll transition projects
  • Change management and stakeholder engagement
  • Identifying organisational capability risks and opportunities
  • Oversight of employee relations frameworks, investigations and grievances
  • Culture, retention and engagement initiatives
  • Workforce reporting and people insights
  • Supporting leaders through organisational growth and transformation
About you
You will be a commercially minded HR professional who enjoys working in environments where priorities shift, timelines move quickly and solutions need to be practical. You will have experience in operated in complex, highly regulated workforce environments and can confidently navigate modern awards, workforce compliance and employee relations risk.
You'll bring:
  • Strong HR Business Partnering or Senior HR Advisory experience within complex, multi-site organisations
  • Demonstrated experience interpreting and applying complex modern awards, with particular interest in candidates who have worked extensively with the SCHADS Award
  • Experience supporting organisational change, acquisitions, integration activity, transformation or growth initiatives
  • Strong employee and industrial relations capability, including investigations, grievances and performance matters
  • A data-led and technology-focused approach, using systems and automation to improve efficiency and scalability
  • Strong project management skills and the ability to manage multiple concurrent priorities
  • Exceptional stakeholder management and influencing capability, particularly where outcomes must be achieved without direct authority
  • The confidence to operate in an environment that is fast paced, evolving and often ambiguous
  • Play a key role in a significant acquisition and growth journey
  • Influence people outcomes across multiple businesses nationally
  • Work closely with senior leaders on strategic initiatives
  • Join a values-led organisation making a meaningful impact in the care sector
  • Broad exposure across integration, change, culture, workforce strategy and governanceGenuine opportunity to shape how a growing organisation scales
This role will suit someone who is entrepreneurial, adaptable and enjoys creating order from complexity. If you're looking for a highly visible HR opportunity where your work directly influences organisational growth and long-term success, Please apply now

job.title: People & Culture Business Partner

Working closely with senior leaders and as part of a national People & Culture function, you will act as the key P&C contact for the South Australian business, balancing strategic partnering with the delivery of pragmatic, commercially focused HR solutions.

The environment is fast-paced and operational, so this opportunity will suit someone who enjoys being close to the business, building credibility with leaders and employees, and taking ownership rather than operating within a highly segmented HR model.

Partnering with leaders across the business, you will provide advice, coaching and support across a diverse range of people matters. You will build trusted stakeholder relationships and help strengthen leadership capability while ensuring national people initiatives are effectively embedded locally.
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Providing operational HR advice and coaching to leaders across the employee lifecycle.
  • Managing complex employee and industrial relations matters, including workplace investigations and performance issues.
  • Playing an active role in enterprise bargaining, including preparation, stakeholder engagement, and implementation.
  • Supporting workforce planning, recruitment, onboarding and retention strategies.
  • Coaching leaders on performance management, development and effective people leadership.
  • Supporting organisational change and transformation initiatives.
  • Providing guidance on employment legislation, industrial instruments, policies and procedures.
  • Contributing to the development and implementation of broader national People & Culture projects and initiatives.
  • Using workforce insights and data to identify trends and support better people and business decisions.
About You
You will be an experienced HR generalist who is comfortable operating autonomously and can move confidently between strategic conversations and hands-on employee matters.

Ideally, you will bring:
  • 3+ years' experience in an HR Business Partner or comparable generalist HR position.
  • Tertiary qualifications in Human Resources, Business Management or a related discipline.
  • Sound knowledge of Australian employment legislation, workplace relations and contemporary HR practices.
  • Practical experience managing employee relations and industrial relations matters.
  • The confidence to coach and influence leaders at different levels of an organisation.
  • Strong stakeholder management, communication and relationship-building capability.
  • The ability to navigate change, ambiguity and sensitive workplace matters with sound judgement.
  • A commercial and pragmatic approach, with the ability to use data and insights to inform decisions.
  • The ability to work independently while remaining closely connected to a broader national HR team.
Experience within transport, logistics, manufacturing, warehousing, infrastructure, engineering or another operational/industrial environment would be particularly valuable.

Why Consider This Opportunity?
This is an excellent opportunity for an HR professional looking for genuine ownership and breadth. Rather than specialising in one area of HR, you will work closely with the business across the full spectrum of people matters, while having access to the expertise and support of a national P&C function.

You will have the opportunity to guide and influence leaders, navigate ER/IR matters, contribute to enterprise bargaining and change initiatives, and help shape the people agenda within the South Australian operation.

If you enjoy being visible in the business, building trusted relationships and delivering practical HR solutions, this is an opportunity to make a tangible impact.
